Updated Developer Context
Project Foundation
PrismaTonal is a touch-first, microtonal synthesizer web application built with React, TypeScript, and Vite. It utilizes a custom Web Audio API architecture for low-latency polyphonic synthesis, supporting Just Intonation lattices, Equal Temperament grids, and other tuning systems. The application prioritizes mobile responsiveness, multitouch interaction, and high-performance visual rendering using HTML5 Canvas.
Audio Architecture
The audio engine is driven by a custom AudioWorkletProcessor (PrismaProcessor) that handles DSP tasks such as oscillator generation (Sine, Saw, Square, Triangle, Noise, Glottal), envelope shaping, filtering, and mixing. It supports dynamic voice allocation, MPE-style pitch bending per voice, and a modular effects chain including reverb, delay, and compression. State management synchronizes React UI controls with the audio thread via a robust messaging system.
Visualization & Interaction
The core visual component, TonalityDiamond, renders a dynamic harmonic lattice where nodes represent pitch ratios. It uses a decoupled rendering loop: heavy geometric calculations (generation, projection) are memoized and throttled in useLatticeData, while the 60fps render loop (LatticeRenderer) handles drawing and animations. Interaction logic manages pointers for tapping, dragging (pitch bend), and latching notes, supporting complex performance techniques like strumming and continuous modulation.
Harmonic Logic
The lattice generation relies on a prime-based coordinate system (Primes 3, 5, 7, 11, 13). Pitch ratios are calculated as fractions and projected into 2D space. The application recently transitioned from a 'Max Prime' filtering logic to an 'Odd Limit' (Identity) classification system. This allows composite identities (e.g., 9-limit, 15-limit) to be filtered and visualized independently, providing more granular control over the harmonic complexity displayed on the lattice.
